p: thee: He prays to God with full assurance of faith, that he will deliver him from his adversaries.
righteousness: By declaring yourself true to your promises.
hast given commandment to save me: You have infinite means and all creatures are at your commandment; therefore show some sign by which I will be delivered.
of the wicked: That is, from Absalom, Ahithophel and that conspiracy.
trust from my youth: He strengthens his faith by the experience of God's benefits, who not only preserved him in his mother's womb, but took him from there, and ever since has preserved him.
wonder unto many: All the world wonders at me because of my miseries: both those in authority and the common people, yet being assured of your favour, I remain steadfast.
old age: You who helped me in my youth when I had more strength, help me now even more in my old age and weakness.
God hath forsaken him: Thus the wicked both blaspheme God and triumph against his saints, as though he had forsaken them if he permits them to fall into their hands.
my God: In calling him his God, he puts back the false reports of the adversaries who said God had forsaken him.
for I know not the numbers: Because your benefits toward me are innumerable, I cannot but continually meditate and rehearse them.
go in the strength of the: I will remain steadfast, being upheld by the power of God.
Now also when I am old: He desires that as he has begun, he would so continue his benefits, that his liberality may have perfect praise.
righteousness also: Your just performance of your promise.
sore troubles: As he confesses that God is the only author of his deliverance, so he acknowledges that these evils were sent to him by God's providence.
truth: He confesses that his long delay was well recompensed, when God performed his promise.
soul: For there is no true praising of God, unless it comes from the heart: and therefore he promises to delight in nothing, except that in which God is glorified.
